what: The Water Intake Calculator estimates how much water to drink each day from your body weight, the minutes of exercise you do, hot weather, and whether you are pregnant or breastfeeding. It shows the total in litres or fluid ounces and as a number of glasses of the size you choose.

It uses a common rule of thumb: about 35 ml per kg of body weight, plus about 350 ml for every 30 minutes of exercise, 500 ml in hot weather, 300 ml in pregnancy and 700 ml while breastfeeding. A breakdown shows each part. A simple tracker lets you tap a glass each time you drink, and remembers today's count in this browser.
This is general guidance, not medical advice. Food and other drinks count too, and people with heart or kidney problems should follow their doctor's advice.
uses: Turn a vague "drink more water" into a clear number of glasses.
See how much extra to drink around a workout or a long walk.
Add the hot weather allowance for summer days or holidays somewhere warm.
Include the extra water often recommended at these times.
Tap glasses as you drink and watch the bar fill up.
tutorial: In "Units", choose "Metric (kg, litres)" or "Imperial (lb, fl oz)".
Type your weight in "Body weight". Results appear as soon as there is a number.
Enter today's exercise in minutes, pick "Hot or humid" if it is hot, and choose Pregnant or Breastfeeding if that applies.
"Glass size" sets how the total is split into glasses, from a 200 ml glass to a 500 ml bottle.
"Water per day", "Glasses per day" and the total in the other unit appear in the boxes, with a breakdown underneath.
Under "Today's tracker", tap a glass (or "+ 1 glass") each time you drink. Tap the last filled glass to undo it. The count is kept for today and starts again tomorrow.
features: Total ml = 35 × weight in kg + 350 × exercise minutes ÷ 30 + 500 if hot + 300 if pregnant or 700 if breastfeeding.
Weight in kg or lb; results in litres or fluid ounces (1 fl oz = 29.57 ml).
Glasses per day = total ÷ glass size, rounded up.
See how much comes from body weight, exercise, heat and pregnancy.
Tap glasses as you drink; the count is saved in this browser for today only and never uploaded.
Your weight and options are kept on this device for next time.

example.title: Worked example: 70 kg with a workout on a hot day
example.text: Body weight: 35 × 70 = 2,450 ml. Thirty minutes of exercise adds 350 ml and hot weather adds 500 ml, for 3,300 ml, shown as 3.3 L. With 250 ml glasses that is 3,300 ÷ 250 = 13.2, rounded up to 14 glasses. On a normal day without exercise the same person gets 2.5 L, or 10 glasses.

tips: Spread your water through the day instead of drinking a lot at once.
Pale yellow urine is a good sign you are drinking enough.
Tea, coffee, milk, soup and fruit all count towards your daily water.
Drink a little extra before, during and after exercise.
If you have a medical condition that limits fluids, follow your doctor's advice instead.
problems: Enter your body weight; the other fields are optional.
It says to check my weight
The calculator is for adults between 20 and 300 kg (45 to 660 lb). Check that the units match your weight.
My tracker went back to zero
The tracker resets every day, and it is stored only in this browser, so another browser or private window starts at zero.
Exercise minutes and hot weather add a lot. Remember food and other drinks also count.
